name: Terrain Tile Ingest Scheduler Nodes
description: The ORCHESTRATION half of the terrain lane. terrain-source is the request-scoped decoder - DEM/WBM bytes in, terrain tiles out, nothing persisted - and this module is the scheduler: pure nodes read a durable $IRM resume mark (through hostcap/flatsql-query), walk the TMS GEOGRAPHIC_WGS84 tile pyramid REGION-PRIORITY ordered (higher priority first, shallow levels before deep), emit bounded plans ($DTT header records) and the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM and water-body granule HttpRequests, author the storage attribution (IngestRequest), and advance the mark only from a verified store (IngestResult -> $IRM for hostcap/storage-write). OCEAN CELLS: Copernicus publishes no granule over open ocean and the guest cannot cheaply know land from ocean, so every intersecting granule is fetched and a 404 is no-data, never an error. The mark doubles as the same-data ledger: the upstream ETag rides on it. TYPED CONTRACTS 1.0: FlatBuffers only - TimerTick, HttpRequest, IngestRequest/IngestResult, FlowNotice and ModuleConfig (module-sdk runtime types), $IRM, $DTT, $FSO and $FSB (SDS) - no JSON and no base64 between modules; node config through plugin.getConfig (SDS $PIV, ConfigEntry list "entries", nested values under dotted keys such as regions.0.west). NO CAPABILITIES: http, storage and flatsql are the generic hostcap connector nodes.

sequentialJustification.detail: Every method is a single-pass transform over the frames the flow hands it: it formats a query, a bounded plan with its requests, an attribution frame or a mark. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (TICK) from the flow's timer trigger; its fields are not read.

inputPorts.description: Cron timer tick (content ignored).

acceptedTypeSets.description: $FSO (OPERATION QUERY_RECORDS) for hostcap/flatsql-query:query: QUERY = config mark_sql (default SELECT _data FROM IRM ORDER BY _rowid DESC LIMIT ?), PARAMETERS one int64 (config mark_scan_rows, default 32) in FlatSQL's tagged encoding, PARAMETER_COUNT 1.

outputPorts.description: The read of this lane's durable $IRM resume mark over the code-named unified view, newest first.

methods.description: Turns the timer tick into the flatsql-query that reads this lane's durable $IRM resume mark back. The relation is the SDS CODE (IRM) over _data/_rowid, which is the only form a current node answers: the old `SELECT * FROM terrain_ingest_mark` named a table no node has, so it read back nothing and every run restarted at cell 0. It is a SEPARATE node from ingest_plan on purpose: the plan takes the mark as an INPUT, and a node that emitted its own input would be a cycle in the flow graph. It emits ONE $FSO QUERY_RECORDS control frame (typed contracts 1.0: no JSON between modules). BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.displayName: Plan a bounded batch of terrain tiles

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (TICK); FIRED_MS (else SCHEDULED_MS) is the run's clock: it dates the edition when config carries no dataset_epoch and is every plan header's RETRIEVED_AT.

inputPorts.description: Cron timer tick.

acceptedTypeSets.description: hostcap/flatsql-query's answer to mark_query: ordered $FSB chunks (CHUNK_SEQUENCE 0..n-1) whose DATA is the aligned size-prefixed $IRM record stream, newest first. The first record whose JOB_ID is dataset@tileset@epoch is this walk's mark (NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX, RECORDS_COMMITTED, SOURCE.ENTITY_TAG); a mark for another job is ignored, an ABANDONED / INVALIDATED one restarts the walk, and a pre-1.0 mark whose DECODER_STATE stamps disagree is refused.

inputPorts.description: The durable resume mark, when one is stored (absent on the first run).

acceptedTypeSets.description: ONE $DTT HEADER record per frame (PAYLOAD present and empty): TILESET_ID, TILING_SCHEME GEOGRAPHIC_WGS84, LEVEL/X/Y and WEST/SOUTH/EAST/NORTH_DEG, PROVENANCE (DATASET_ID, DATASET_NAME, DATASET_EPOCH, RETRIEVED_AT the run's clock, LICENSE, LICENSE_URL, ATTRIBUTION; SOURCE_QUERY = the elevation granule URLs the tile needs, space-separated), WATER_MASK_PROVENANCE.SOURCE_QUERY = the water-body granule URLs, ETAG = the mark's upstream entity tag (the If-None-Match its granule fetches present), REMARKS region and tile index. A 404 on any of those granules is open ocean, never an error.

outputPorts.description: One work unit per frame: the tile, the granules it needs, the provenance. At most batch_tiles (default 64, clamped to 256) frames per invocation; the remainder is reported as backlog.

acceptedTypeSets.description: The job: the $IRM this batch will make durable once it is stored - JOB_ID dataset@tileset@epoch, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE (SOURCE_URL the granule base, SOURCE_VERSION the edition), STATE IN_PROGRESS, RANGE_MODE PART_INDEX, LAST_CHUNK.CHUNK_INDEX the batch's first index, NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX that index plus the batch's stride, RECORDS_COMMITTED what the resumed mark had committed, UPDATED_AT the run's clock, TAGS lane:terrain + walk:cell|tile, NOTES region/level/cell/tiles. Stride: the batch's tile count.

outputPorts.description: The run contract for this batch.

methods.description: SUPERSEDED BY granule_plan FOR PYRAMID BUILDS (2026-08-26): this lane emits one plan frame per TILE, which cannot feed an encoder that amortizes a granule decode across every tile the granule covers - it re-fetches and re-decodes the same granule about 130 times per 1-degree cell at z11. It is kept for a caller that genuinely wants one tile per fetch and is slated for removal once the pyramid lane is live. ONE INVOCATION IS ONE BOUNDED BATCH. The plan walks the TMS GEOGRAPHIC_WGS84 pyramid (2x1 level-0 roots, row origin SOUTH) REGION-PRIORITY ordered: regions by priority descending (config order breaks ties), shallow levels before deep within a region, tiles row-major within a level. That order is a pure function of the config, so a tile's global index is stable and the durable mark is a single integer - the next tile to plan. At most batch_tiles (default 64) plan frames are emitted per invocation and the remainder is reported through the backlog counter, so the runtime re-invokes until the pyramid drains. Granule lists are the tile extent CLIPPED to the region bbox, expanded to whole-degree cells: a level-0 tile intersects tens of thousands of 1-degree granules, and the ones outside the region render from the ellipsoid either way. Every intersecting granule is planned (as a header's SOURCE_QUERY) because Copernicus publishes NO object for open-ocean cells and the guest cannot cheaply know land from ocean; a 404 is no-data, never an error. Fails closed with no tileset_id or an empty regions list rather than inventing a whole-earth plan. A mark for a different dataset, tileset or epoch is ignored; a drained enumeration is a clean no-op. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. TYPED CONTRACTS 1.0: TimerTick and $FSB mark in; $DTT header records and an $IRM job out.

methods.description: THE GRANULE-MAJOR PLANNER, and the one the pyramid builder runs. ingest_plan is TILE-MAJOR: one plan frame per tile, each naming the granules that tile needs. That was the right shape when the encoder decoded per tile and it is the wrong shape now that it does not - the encoder amortizes a granule decode across every tile the granule covers, and a tile-major plan can never hand it more than one tile at a time. A z11 tile is 0.088 degrees and a granule is a whole degree, so tile-major planning re-fetches and re-decodes the SAME granule about 130 times per cell. This planner inverts it: the unit of work is ONE GRANULE CELL at one level. The 2x2 granule neighbourhood is fetched (four elevation + four water-body HttpRequests, ALWAYS exactly four so the flow's http nodes are fed unconditionally; longitude wraps, latitude clamps) and ONE plan frame carries every tile of that level whose SOUTH-WEST CORNER falls in the cell. The south-west corner is the assignment rule for a reason: a tile so assigned extends at most one tile-span north and east, so its extent lies inside the 2x2 neighbourhood and NEVER needs a third cell - assigning by tile CENTRE would reach into the west and south neighbours too and make the granule set 3x3. LEVEL FLOOR: that argument holds only while a tile is no wider than a granule, which is level 8 (180/2^8 = 0.703 degrees) and deeper. Shallower levels need many granules per tile and are built by DOWNSAMPLING deeper tiles over the record store, a different lane; a plan that asks this one for them is REFUSED with error code "level-below-granule-floor" rather than served tiles with most of their extent missing. The enumeration - regions by priority, then level, then cell row-major - is a pure function of the config, so the durable mark stays a single integer: the next CELL index. Cells the region bbox clips to nothing are skipped rather than fetched to build zero tiles. Fails closed without tileset_id, dataset_epoch, a retrieved_at (config or tick) or a non-empty regions list. BATCHING: every input port is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE; maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind, so a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames". TYPED CONTRACTS 1.0: TimerTick and $FSB mark in; HttpRequests, a $DTT header stream, a ModuleConfig of encoder options and an $IRM job out - no JSON, no responseWire/allow_404 dialect (a granule's body is verbatim in its HttpResponse and a 404 is read by the encoder as ocean).

acceptedTypeSets.description: The planner's $IRM job (the mark-to-be): JOB_ID names dataset@tileset@epoch, LAST_CHUNK.CHUNK_INDEX the batch's first index, SOURCE.SOURCE_URL the granule base.

methods.description: Authors the attribution the storage lane cannot invent - dataset, tileset, batch and epoch - and forwards the tile records untouched. The batch id is tileset_id@dataset_epoch#first_tile_index, so re-running a batch is idempotent at the storage lane and two batches never collide. RECONCILE is None (append) because a batch is a WINDOW of the pyramid, never the tileset's complete set - a source-batch reconcile on it would delete every tile outside the window. REFUSES a job whose JOB_ID does not name dataset, tileset and epoch ("incomplete-job-attribution"): the epoch is the edition boundary and storage cannot invent the edition a tile belongs to. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned would destroy every other frame it was handed. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. TYPED CONTRACTS 1.0: $IRM job, $DTT records, FlowNotice report and HttpResponse in; IngestRequest and $DTT records out.

acceptedTypeSets.description: THE DURABLE RESUME MARK: the job completed from the VERIFIED store result - RECORDS_COMMITTED += INSERTED, LAST_CHUNK.BATCH_ID / RECORDS_STORED / COMMITTED_AT, SEQUENCE and CHUNKS_COMMITTED = NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX, SOURCE.ENTITY_TAG / LAST_MODIFIED from the provenance, STATE COMPLETE (and COMPLETED_AT) when the cell walk is done. For hostcap/storage-write (record) and egress. Not emitted for a refused batch or for inserted=0 over a batch that carried tiles.

outputPorts.description: The advanced resume mark ($IRM).

acceptedTypeSets.description: The dataset-publication POST (publish_url): content-type application/octet-stream, BODY an IngestResult naming the stored batch (SCHEMA, PROVIDER_ID, SOURCE_NAME, BATCH_ID, INSERTED ...). Emitted ONLY when publish_url is configured.

outputPorts.description: Dataset-publication POST announcing this batch.

methods.description: Advances the resume mark from the STORAGE RESULT, never at dispatch. THE DURABLE MARK IS AN $IRM RECORD - the planner's job completed from the verified result - written through hostcap/storage-write (record port; the old JSON meta port is gone, the type is the frame's own) and read back through the code-named FlatSQL view; the same $IRM lands on egress for an operator. A mark advanced at plan time turns a crash between fetch and store into a permanently skipped batch of tiles, and the hole is invisible. A batch storage REFUSED is an error (ingest-refused) and the mark does not move; the silent nop - inserted=0 for a batch that carried tiles - is refused the same way (ingest-stored-nothing). The publication POST (an IngestResult FlatBuffer body) is fail-closed: emitted ONLY when publish_url is configured, and the mark is NOT gated on it. TYPED CONTRACTS 1.0: IngestResult, IngestRequest and $IRM in; $IRM and HttpRequest out. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE; a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".

methods.description: A body's planner (GEOGRAPHIC_TWO_ROOT_BODY on the body's reference sphere; config body: moon (default) or mars, each a table of its PDS products and default caps). Moon: NASA LRO LOLA gridded products (public domain), ldem_4 L0-3, ldem_16 L4-5, ldem_64 L6-7 global, ldem_75{s,n}_240m L8 |lat| >= 75, ldem_75{s,n}_120m L9 |lat| >= 80, ldem_75s_60m L10 lat <= -85. Mars: NASA MGS MOLA MEGDR (public domain), megr 4 ppd L0-3, 16 ppd L4-5, 32 ppd L6, 64 ppd (4 files) L7, 128 ppd (16 files, to 88 degrees) L8 within 87.1875, the 512 ppd polar products L8 beyond 87.1875, L9 beyond 78.75 and L10 beyond 84.375. A tile is built from a cap (config caps) only when its whole extent lies inside the band. Unit 0 is every tile of levels 0-2 (the root file); after it, per cap and level, a simple cylindrical product is walked one BLOCK ROW (four tile rows; runs of at most 64 blocks by longitude) per unit, reading the lines from every file of the product they cross, and a polar product by whole 4x4 blocks sorted by the first image line their footprint touches, at most 64 blocks and max_range_bytes (default 72 MiB) of lines per unit, so every packed block file is complete in one unit. Each file is asked for as its label then range_parts whole-line ranges (If-Match on its ETag), at most 16 requests (dem_0..dem_15); the enumeration is a pure function of the config, so the $IRM mark is one integer (the next unit). A drained walk is a clean no-op.

acceptedTypeSets.description: hostcap/flatsql-query's answer to mark_query: ordered $FSB chunks (CHUNK_SEQUENCE 0..n-1) whose DATA is the aligned size-prefixed $IRM record stream, newest first. The first record whose JOB_ID is dataset@tileset@epoch is this walk's mark (NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX, RECORDS_COMMITTED, SOURCE.ENTITY_TAG); a mark for another job is ignored, an ABANDONED / INVALIDATED one restarts the walk, and a pre-1.0 mark whose DECODER_STATE stamps disagree is refused.

methods.description: THE IMPORT: a body's terrain walk encoded elsewhere by the same modules (terrain-ingest:body_plan, terrain-source:tile and pack) and published here. Plans the walk's own unit with body_plan's config (body, tileset_id, dataset_epoch, caps, max_grid_size, max_range_bytes, path_prefix) at the import's own mark, never below import_from_unit, and asks import_base_url for the finished files of as many consecutive units as fit one host-adapter call (import_max_files, default and at most 32 files; a unit is never split), planned in one pass over the ladder. A drained import is a clean no-op.
